title: Pin-and-deploy walkthrough + microcopy snapshots
body:
Purpose:
This is a working walkthrough capturing microcopy variants, quick ASCII wireframe snapshots, and grooming notes for the model catalog -> endpoint creation -> model version pin flow. The focus: make the flow feel low-friction for engineers while surfacing cost/latency tradeoffs and rollback safety.

Summary of intent:
- Single-screen primary path for simple deploys (pin latest stable, choose instance profile, create endpoint)
- Secondary, expandable advanced panel for rollouts (canary %, multi-version pin, fallback rules)
- Inline cost + latency estimates updated based on model/quant profile and batch window
- Microcopy explicitly reassures: "non-destructive by default; you can rollback"

Wireframe snapshots (quick ASCII sketches, intended to be translated into high-fidelity frames):

[SCREEN: Create endpoint (compact)]
-------------------------------------------------------------
| Title: Create endpoint — Quick deploy                       |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| Model selector [Search model or paste model-id] v           |
| Selected: redwood/vicuna-2.1 (quantized-8bit) [pin-> latest] |
| Model metadata:  800M params | est latency: ~95ms | est $/1k toks: $0.08 |
| Instance profile: [nvidia-a10] v   | Concurrency: [default auto] |
| Toggle: Advanced options v                                    |
| Button: Create endpoint  | Button: Cancel                     |
-------------------------------------------------------------

Advanced panel (collapsed by default):
- Canary rollout: slider 0-100% (0 = disabled)
- Fallback model: dropdown (compatible variants only)
- Pin strategy: Latest | SemVer | Commit-hash (text input)
- KV cache toggle and TTL setting

Microcopy draft (primary candidates) — short and long forms so UX can choose context-appropriate text:
- Primary CTA (short): "Create endpoint"
- Primary CTA (with reinforcement): "Create endpoint — non-destructive"
- Helper under model selector: "Pin a model version so your endpoint is stable. You can update or rollback later."
- Cheap reassurance for novices: "Pins are logical labels — they don't overwrite your model. Use canary to test changes."
- Cost/latency tooltip: "Estimated per-request latency and cost are based on past traffic patterns for this model and selected instance profile. Actuals may vary."

Microcopy alternatives for the pin input label (A/B test candidates):
A) "Pin version (recommended for production): [Latest | Tag | Hash]"
B) "Model version to serve — leave blank to serve latest"
C) "Choose a stable model version (you can change without downtime)"

Copy for rollback/upgrade confirmation modal (when user updates a pin):
Title: "Update model for endpoint 'payments-qa'"
Body (short): "This endpoint will start serving model redwood/gptx-3.2 (v2026-02-25). Traffic will switch according to your rollout settings. You can rollback from endpoint settings."
Body (detailed): "Rolling forward is non-destructive: we create a new revision behind the scenes and switch routing rules. Rolling back replaces routing rules to the previous revision. If you enabled canary, only a subset of requests will hit the new model until you confirm."
Buttons: [Start rollout] [Cancel]

Accessibility notes (a11y):
- Ensure 'pin version' input has clear aria-describedby linking to the helper copy.
- Slider for canary must support keyboard increments (1% step) and numeric input box.
- Color usage for risk indicators (e.g., red label for 'breaking change detection') needs text alternatives.

Edge cases and UX decisions to resolve in grooming:
1) What happens if selected model variant is incompatible with chosen instance profile? (Current draft: block and show quick fix button: "Switch instance profile to compatible GPU")
2) Multiple users updating pin concurrently -> last-writer wins or optimistic lock? Suggestion: optimistic lock + toast: "This endpoint was updated 2 min ago by Priya. Review changes? [View diff]"
3) Large model (multi-GPU) deploys should show staging window estimate (provision time) and optional warmup flag.
4) If model quantization reduces quality risk, show small 'quality delta' badge with link to evaluation results.

Backlog grooming items (prioritized):
- INF-201: Add live cost/latency estimate API endpoint to power the estimate row (P0 for UX parity).
- INF-202: Wire up canary slider with backend routing flags + metric hooks (P0).
- UX-334: Implement optimistic locking + diff view for concurrent pin updates (P1).
- DOCS-87: Create short-runbook copy for "how to rollback a pin" and surface in inline help (P1).
- QA-59: E2E test for pin-to-rollback path including canary and fallback.

Implementation notes for engineers (short):
- Frontend: keep the quick path as a single POST with minimal body; advanced options should be a nested payload fragment so backend accepts an abbreviated create request.
- Backend: endpoint creation should return a provisioning job id; client polls and shows a provisioning toast.
- Telemetry: emit events for pin_change.requested, pin_change.completed, pin_change.rollback_requested with metadata: user_id, endpoint_id, from_version, to_version.

Design tradeoffs considered (rationale):
- Minimal primary screen reduces cognitive load for first-time users. Most customers want to deploy quickly.
- Advanced options hidden but discoverable — avoids scaring novice devs while still enabling power users.
- Show cost/latency estimates early to reduce surprise bill shock when scaling.

Open questions for PM/Eng review (please respond inline):
- How precise must the cost estimate be? (rounded to 2 significant figures vs. real-time billing calc)
- Do we want default pin strategy to be 'Latest stable tag' or empty to implicitly pick latest?
- Should canary be enabled in the quick flow with a tiny default (5%) or always off?

Quick QA checklist for next review meeting:
- [ ] Microcopy alternatives A/B flagged in feature flags
- [ ] Accessibility checks for sliders and helper text
- [ ] Backend readiness: estimate API exists (INF-201)
- [ ] Telemetry hooks implemented and validated

Appendix: example API payloads (informal) — these are suggestions to keep frontend simple:
- Quick create (minimal):
  {
    "endpoint_name": "payments-qa",
    "model_id": "redwood/vicuna-2.1:latest",
    "instance_profile": "a10-small"
  }

- Full create (advanced):
  {
    "endpoint_name": "payments-qa",
    "model_id": "redwood/gptx-3.2:v2026-02-25",
    "instance_profile": "a100-4x",
    "canary_pct": 10,
    "fallback_model": "redwood/gptx-3.2:previous",
    "kv_cache": { "enabled": true, "ttl_secs": 3600 }
  }

Notes-to-self: capture sample screenshots from design later and replace ASCII snapshots. Schedule 30m sync with backend next Tue to align on job provisioning shape.

-- end of doc --
